A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HUG and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material. The complete documents support reliable comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original HUG reconstruction results on four scenes, component ablations, rendering-efficiency measurements, and supplementary partitioning analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports original HUG results on five scenes, partitioning and optimization timings, and cumulative ablations. Its disclosure that some baseline scores come from prior papers does not affect the originality of HUG's results.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 replaces view selection by mask area exceeding 10% with selection by visible sparse-point counts exceeding 800. Section 3.4 changes fusion filtering: v1 can discard an inside-block anchor with fewer than two inside Gaussians, whereas v2 retains inside-block anchors and additionally preserves outside anchors receiving majority votes. These change the procedure; the hierarchical weighted loss itself is retained.

E1.justification: v2 adds Sci-Art to the retained MatrixCity, Residence, Rubble, and Building scenes for the same aerial novel-view-synthesis task. The dedicated increasing-camera-height evaluation from v1 Figure 5 is absent.

E2.justification: v2 adds Hier-GS to quantitative and qualitative comparisons and adds VastGS to Table 1 and the partitioning comparison. VastGaussian already appeared in v1's supplementary qualitative comparisons, so it is not entirely new. The CityGS-LOD comparator disappears with the rendering-efficiency experiment.

E3.justification: The evaluation design changes from Building leave-one-component-out ablations to cumulative component additions on Rubble, and introduces multi-method partitioning and optimization timing comparisons. The camera-height/FPS protocol is removed. v2 also reports fourfold downsampling for real scenes instead of v1's 1.6k-resolution description; the PDFs do not establish that these settings are equivalent.

E4.justification: v1 Table 2 separately removes splitting/pruning, hierarchical supervision, and focused training. v2 Table 3 instead progressively adds masking, hierarchical supervision, and dynamic gradient thresholds. The camera-height sensitivity analysis is removed, while partitioning analysis expands to VastGS. The unoptimized-anchor case study is retained and moved from supplementary Figure 10 to main Figure 5.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Both present point estimates without statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes HUG's real-scene scores, including Rubble PSNR from 25.80 to 26.42 and LPIPS from 0.247 to 0.197, while retaining MatrixCity scores. Sci-Art, additional comparator scores, timings, and replacement ablation results are added. v2 ties CityGS's Residence SSIM at 0.813 and trails Mega-NeRF on Sci-Art PSNR, 21.83 versus 25.60. Revised methods and reported preprocessing prevent treating cross-version differences as controlled same-setting gains.

T1.justification: v2 replaces the mask-area selection inequality with an indicator-based visible-point membership rule and introduces the explicit cumulative, bounded anchor-level update in Equation 9. The Gaussian definitions, distance-based LOD equations, and hierarchical loss remain substantively unchanged. Neither version provides theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claim of efficient block-based reconstruction using hierarchical neural Gaussians remains. v2 narrows the stated scope to aerial urban scenes and makes approximately one-minute visibility-based partitioning an explicit main contribution. The generic state-of-the-art claim is retained, with broader supporting evaluations.

C2.justification: v2 adds the limitation that integrated aerial-ground training and rendering are unsupported, while omitting v1's explicit lighting-inconsistency limitation. It tentatively attributes the Sci-Art PSNR shortfall to distant views and explains VastGS's missing MatrixCity quantitative results through excessive view assignments and GPU memory limits.

D1.justification: New supplementary Section 6 identifies baseline-score sources, released checkpoints, default Hier-GS settings, and an unofficial VastGS implementation. v2 also specifies beta = 4. Conversely, it omits v1's staged training-iteration budget, SVM downsampling and weighting details, and promised HUG code/data/preprocessing release statement. These substantially change reproducibility documentation without establishing resource availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds the hierarchical 3D Gaussian representation paper underlying Hier-GS and removes the support-vector-networks reference. It also drops v1's specific contrast with GigaGS discarding neural anchors after training. Most related-work coverage and positioning remain.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, substantial method explanations, experimental discussion, and supplementary narrative are extensively rewritten or reorganized. Method subsections are renamed and regrouped, and baseline settings replace the supplementary visibility-mask discussion. The title gains an aerial-scene qualifier and the first two authors exchange order.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the pipeline and annotates the hierarchical-supervision diagram, expands qualitative comparison grids, enlarges Table 1, and introduces a timing table. It replaces the ablation display, removes the FPS/Gaussian-count plots and visibility-mask illustration, revises partitioning radar plots, and relocates the retained anchor-artifact example into the main text.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the empirical case through relevant Hier-GS/VastGS comparisons, five-scene timing evidence, and explicit baseline provenance. These improve assessment of the method beyond higher reported scores alone. The net gain is limited by removal of the camera-height/FPS analysis and important training and SVM implementation details, which weakens reproducibility and evidence for rendering efficiency.
